result.description:
We are looking for a curious and analytically driven Data Scientist to join our team and transform complex datasets into actionable insights that inform strategic decision-making. This role sits at the intersection of mathematics, statistics, programming, and business intelligence, requiring a candidate who can build and deploy sophisticated analytical frameworks including machine learning and AI solutions. The ideal candidate is a collaborative problem-solver with strong communication skills, capable of translating data-driven findings into clear recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
Collect, prepare, and clean large datasets for analysis, identifying and resolving data anomalies, inconsistencies, and quality issues to ensure analytical integrity
Apply advanced analytical techniques drawing on mathematical, statistical, programming, and database skills to extract meaningful insights from structured and unstructured data
Design, build, and deploy machine learning and artificial intelligence frameworks that support automation, prediction, and pattern recognition across business functions
Develop, evaluate, and iteratively refine statistical models and algorithms to uncover trends, forecast outcomes, and generate actionable insights
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand business objectives and translate them into clearly defined data science problems and analytical solutions
Present data-driven findings, visualisations, and recommendations to key decision-makers and stakeholders in a clear and compelling manner
Contribute strategic input and innovation to the organisation's data science roadmap, identifying opportunities to leverage data for competitive advantage
Maintain and document data pipelines, modelling processes, and analytical methodologies to ensure reproducibility and knowledge sharing across the team
Monitor and assess the performance of deployed models, implementing updates and improvements as required to maintain accuracy and relevance
Support data governance and ensure compliance with data privacy regulations and organisational data management policies
Required Qualifications & Skills
Bachelor's degree or higher in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related discipline
Demonstrated experience in a data science or advanced analytics role, with a portfolio of applied projects
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R, with experience in data manipulation libraries (e.g. pandas, NumPy) and machine learning frameworks (e.g. scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch)
Strong understanding of statistical modelling, machine learning algorithms, and data mining techniques
Experience working with large datasets and familiarity with SQL and database querying
Ability to develop and evaluate predictive models, performing validation, tuning, and performance assessment
Proficiency in data visualisation tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or equivalent libraries (e.g. Matplotlib, Seaborn)
Strong analytical thinking with the ability to translate complex findings into clear, business-relevant insights
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with experience presenting to non-technical audiences
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and contribute effectively within a collaborative team environment
Preferred Qualifications
Postgraduate qualification (Master's or PhD) in a quantitative or data-related field
Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud, particularly for model deployment and data storage
Familiarity with MLOps practices and tools for model versioning, monitoring, and deployment pipelines
Knowledge of natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, or other specialist machine learning domains
Experience working within Agile or Scrum delivery frameworks
Relevant industry certifications in data science, machine learning, or cloud computing (e.g. AWS Certified Machine Learning, Google Professional Data Engineer)
Prior experience in a relevant industry sector such as finance, healthcare, retail, or government
Why Join Us?
Be part of a forward-thinking team that places data and innovation at the core of strategic decision-making, giving you meaningful impact from day one
Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for further study, certifications, and attendance at industry conferences
Enjoy a flexible working environment with hybrid arrangements that support a healthy work-life balance
Competitive remuneration package with superannuation and opportunities for performance-based progression
Collaborative and inclusive workplace culture that values diverse perspectives and encourages knowledge sharing
Job Details
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

result.description:
Position: Automotive Technician (Motor Mechanic)
Type: Full-time
Employer: JG Prestige Auto Pty Ltd
Location: Clayton South VIC
Salary: $79,560 per annum
About the Business:
JG Prestige Auto Pty Ltd is an independent specialist workshop in Clayton South dedicated to Mercedes-Benz and other European vehicles. We deliver dealership-standard diagnostics, mechanical repairs, auto electrical work, air conditioning services and logbook servicing using advanced diagnostic equipment and high-grade parts. Our reputation is built on honest diagnosis, transparent upfront pricing, quality workmanship and a 24-month/20,000 km warranty. We value precision, clear communication and genuine customer care in a professional, well-equipped workshop environment that prioritises accuracy over shortcuts.
About the Position:
The Automotive Technician (Motor Mechanic) is responsible for diagnosing, maintaining and repairing Mercedes-Benz and European vehicles to a high technical standard. This hands-on role is central to delivering reliable, dealership-level service without the dealership price tag, ensuring vehicles leave the workshop performing safely and smoothly while supporting the growth of a specialist independent business.
Key Responsibilities:
Diagnose mechanical and electrical faults using advanced diagnostic equipment (including Xentry/ISTA and similar systems) and interpret live data and fault codes accurately.
Perform scheduled logbook servicing and routine maintenance to manufacturer specifications.
Repair and replace components including engines, transmissions, braking systems, steering, suspension, cooling systems, clutches and related mechanical assemblies.
Carry out auto electrical repairs, battery/charging system diagnostics, and air conditioning inspections, leak testing and re-gassing.
Dismantle, inspect, repair or replace worn or defective parts and reassemble components to correct specifications, referring to service manuals and technical data.
Road-test vehicles where required and verify repairs meet performance and safety standards.
Maintain a clean, organised and safe workshop environment, complete job cards accurately and communicate findings clearly to the business owner/customers.
Source and fit OEM or equivalent high-grade parts and support transparent quoting processes.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in Automotive Technology, Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology, or an equivalent recognised qualification.
Minimum 4 years’ experience as a qualified Automotive Technician / Motor Mechanic.
Strong technical skills in diagnosing and repairing modern European vehicles, including familiarity with electronic control systems and diagnostic software.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving ability, clear communication skills and a professional, customer-focused approach.
Ability to work independently, follow manufacturer procedures, and maintain high standards of workmanship and workshop safety.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

ICBM SERVICES PTY LTD is hiring a Full-time Construction Project Manager role across NSW, WA in Australia. Apply now to be part of our team.

Requirements for this role:

Flexible hours available
2–3 years of relevant work experience required for this role
ICBM SERVICES PTY LTD is looking for an experienced Construction Project Manager for our client’s construction projects, including residential homes, commercial buildings, civil works and public spaces in Sydney.
On a full-time basis, you will be responsible for planning, organising, directing, controlling and coordinating construction projects, as well as managing the physical, financial and human resources involved in the construction process.

Title: Construction Project Manager, Full-time position
Salary: A$ 90,000.00 to 98,000.00 plus super
Work Location: In person
We are looking for applicants who demonstrate the following:

Requirements

•	Bachelor’s degree or higher in Construction Project Management, Construction Management, Building Technology, Building Science, Civil Engineering or another highly relevant field. 
•	At least 2–3 years of relevant experience managing residential, commercial, industrial or civil construction projects. 
•	Demonstrated experience managing construction schedules, budgets, labour, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building legislation, Australian Standards, quality requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Ability to read, assess and interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications and construction contracts. 
•	Experience coordinating architects, engineers, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers, tradespeople and relevant authorities. 
•	Strong understanding of tendering, procurement, contract administration and project cost control. 
•	Ability to identify project risks, delays and budget variations and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
•	Excellent organisational, reporting and problem-solving abilities. 
•	Current Australian driver licence preferred. 
•	Relevant registration, licence or site accreditation may be required depending on the project and scope of work. 

Construction Project Manager Responsibilities

•	Plan, organise, direct, control and coordinate construction projects from commencement through to completion. 
•	Establish project plans, construction schedules, milestones, budgets and resource requirements. 
•	Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, technical specifications and contractual requirements. 
•	Determine appropriate construction methods, sequencing, labour requirements, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Coordinate the procurement and delivery of construction materials, equipment and services. 
•	Consult with architects, engineers, building professionals, consultants, tradespeople and technical workers. 
•	Negotiate and communicate with building owners, property developers, clients, suppliers and subcontractors. 
•	Prepare, review and contribute to tenders, quotations, contract bids and project proposals. 
•	Implement coordinated work programs across construction sites. 
•	Monitor project progress, expenditure, quality, safety, risk and compliance against approved plans and budgets. 
•	Ensure construction activities comply with relevant building legislation, Australian Standards, contractual requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Manage and monitor the performance, quality and progress of contractors and subcontractors. 
•	Arrange the submission of plans, permits and supporting documents to relevant authorities. 
•	Coordinate required inspections, approvals and project handover activities. 
•	Prepare progress reports, budget updates, risk assessments and project documentation. 
•	Identify potential delays, cost overruns, quality issues and construction risks and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Lead and supervise site managers, project engineers, supervisors, forepersons, subcontractors and tradespeople as required. 
•	Maintain effective communication with clients and key stakeholders throughout the construction process. 
•	Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, within budget and in accordance with the required quality standards. 

These responsibilities reflect the official ANZSCO functions for Construction Project Managers, including management of construction schedules, procurement, contractors, budgets, compliance, inspections and project resources. 
If you would like to discuss the role further, please click APPLY and send through an up-to-date CV. We can schedule a time to discuss the position available and determine whether the role is suitable for your qualifications and experience.
Work Location: In person
